title: The documentation framework that makes an LTCF or terminal-illness partial fill lawful
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.13(c) the pharmacist MUST RECORD ON THE PRESCRIPTION whether the patient is 'terminally ill' or an 'LTCF patient', and A PARTIALLY FILLED PRESCRIPTION THAT DOES NOT CARRY THAT NOTATION SHALL BE DEEMED TO HAVE BEEN FILLED IN VIOLATION OF THE ACT. If there is any question whether a patient may be classified as terminally ill the pharmacist must CONTACT THE PRACTITIONER BEFORE partially filling, and pharmacist and prescribing practitioner carry a CORRESPONDING RESPONSIBILITY to assure the substance is for a terminally ill patient. For EACH partial filling the dispensing pharmacist shall record, on the back of the prescription or on another appropriate uniformly maintained and readily retrievable record, the DATE of the partial filling, the QUANTITY DISPENSED, the REMAINING QUANTITY AUTHORIZED to be dispensed, and the IDENTIFICATION OF THE DISPENSING PHARMACIST. The total dispensed in all partial fillings must not exceed the total quantity prescribed.
exam_relevance: Tests the content of the special pathway's documentation rather than its existence, including that the missing 'terminally ill' or 'LTCF patient' notation is itself a violation.

authority.name: Partial filling for LTCF residents and terminally ill patients

exceptions: The notation duty is not a formality: 21 CFR 1306.13(c) deems a partially filled prescription without it filled in violation of the Act.
Where terminal-illness status is uncertain the practitioner must be contacted before the partial fill, not after it.
common_confusions: Naming the special pathway's documentation framework without knowing that it turns on recording 'terminally ill' or 'LTCF patient' on the prescription itself.
Recording only date and quantity and omitting the remaining quantity authorized and the dispensing pharmacist's identification.
Assuming the 60-day outer limit is the only constraint the pathway imposes.
